units.title: Beef and Pork Fabrication Overview
units.summary: Primal and subprimal cuts: where they come from and how to cook them.
units.objective: Identify the major beef and pork primals, name common subprimals, and match each to an appropriate cooking method.
units.cip: CIP 12.0508 – Meat fabrication (alignment to be confirmed by instructor)
miniLesson: A primal is a large initial cut from the carcass. A subprimal is a smaller cut taken from a primal, and portions are cut from subprimals. Fabricating your own primals can lower cost and improve control over portion size and trim.

Location predicts tenderness. Muscles along the back that do little work (loin and rib) are tender. Muscles that support and move the animal (chuck, brisket, shank, round) have more connective tissue.
Safety first: use sharp, appropriate knives, cut-resistant gloves where required, a stable cutting surface, and keep raw meat cold and separated from ready-to-eat foods.

definitions.text: A major section of the carcass, such as the beef rib or pork loin.
A smaller cut from a primal, such as the beef strip loin from the short loin.
Breaking down large cuts into smaller portions.
The usable amount after trimming, bones and waste are removed.

table.caption: Beef and pork primals – visual reference table

knowledgeCheck.stem: Which beef primal contains the ribeye?
knowledgeCheck.explanation: The ribeye roll comes from the rib primal.

knowledgeCheck.stem: Which pork primal is the source of bacon?
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Bacon is cured (and usually smoked) pork belly.

knowledgeCheck.stem: Why are cuts from the chuck usually braised?

options.text: They contain lots of connective tissue from hard-working muscles
They are too small for dry heat

knowledgeCheck.explanation: Hard-working shoulder muscles are tough and need long moist heat to tenderize.

options.text: A finished portion on the plate
A smaller cut taken from a primal

knowledgeCheck.stem: When fabricating raw meat, which practice reduces cross-contamination?

options.text: Use one board for raw meat and ready-to-eat food
Clean and sanitize boards, knives and hands after handling raw meat
Rinse the knife with cold water only
Wipe the board with a dry towel

knowledgeCheck.explanation: Surfaces and tools must be cleaned and sanitized between tasks; do not share boards between raw meat and ready-to-eat foods.

units.title: ServSafe Manager Scenario Practice
units.summary: Realistic kitchen situations: spot the violation and choose the corrective action.
units.objective: Identify food safety violations in realistic scenarios and select appropriate corrective actions.
units.cip: CIP 12.0508 – Food safety and sanitation management (alignment to be confirmed by instructor)
miniLesson: Managers prevent foodborne illness by controlling time and temperature, preventing cross-contamination, enforcing personal hygiene, and cleaning and sanitizing correctly.
The values in the reference table follow the FDA Food Code. Your jurisdiction may adopt a different edition, so the instructor must verify these against the code in effect locally.
These scenarios are original practice items, not official ServSafe exam questions. Official certification practice is available from ServSafe.

definitions.text: Food that requires time/temperature control for safety, such as cooked rice, cut melon, meat and dairy.
The transfer of harmful microorganisms from one food or surface to another.
A step taken to fix a problem and prevent it from causing harm.
The range of temperatures where bacteria multiply fastest.

table.caption: Reference values (FDA Food Code – instructor to verify current local edition)
rows: Do not reheat in hot-holding equipment

scenarios.title: Raw chicken and salad
scenarios.situation: A cook cuts raw chicken on a board, then uses the same board and knife, wiped with a damp towel, to slice tomatoes for a salad.

options.text: Cross-contamination from raw poultry to a ready-to-eat food

questions.explanation: Raw poultry can carry harmful bacteria. Sharing an unsanitized board and knife transfers it to a food that will not be cooked.

questions.stem: What is the best corrective action?

options.text: Discard the tomatoes, then wash, rinse and sanitize the board and knife and use separate equipment
Rinse the tomatoes under cold water

questions.explanation: Contaminated ready-to-eat food must be discarded and surfaces cleaned and sanitized. Prevent recurrence with separate, color-coded equipment.

scenarios.title: The walk-in cooler
scenarios.situation: During a delivery check, a manager measures the internal temperature of cut melon in the cooler at 50°F (10°C). The cooler thermometer reads 49°F.

options.text: Cut melon is not stored in the cooler
A TCS food is being held above the cold-holding temperature

questions.explanation: Cut melon is a TCS food and must be held at 41°F (5°C) or lower.

questions.stem: What should the manager do first?

options.text: Evaluate how long the food has been out of temperature, take action on the food per policy, and fix or service the cooler
Add more melon to the cooler
Turn the thermometer to a lower number

questions.explanation: Determine time out of temperature, discard or act on affected food per policy, then correct the equipment issue and document it.

scenarios.title: Handwashing
scenarios.situation: A cook returns from a break, touches his phone, and starts plating food without washing his hands.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the violation and the correction?

options.text: Hands must be washed at a hand sink before handling food; stop work and wash
Use hand sanitizer instead of washing

questions.explanation: Hands must be washed after breaks and after touching contaminated items such as phones. Gloves do not replace handwashing.

questions.stem: Which is the best long-term fix?

options.text: Retrain staff on when to wash hands and keep sinks stocked and accessible

questions.explanation: A manager prevents repeat problems through training, monitoring and accessible supplies.

knowledgeCheck.explanation: Cooked rice supports bacterial growth if held improperly, so it needs time and temperature control.

knowledgeCheck.stem: At what temperature or colder should TCS food be held cold, per the FDA Food Code?
knowledgeCheck.explanation: The FDA Food Code sets cold holding at 41°F (5°C) or lower. Verify your local code edition.

options.text: Store raw meat above ready-to-eat food
Store ready-to-eat food above raw meat
Store them side by side uncovered
Store them together in one pan

knowledgeCheck.explanation: Raw animal foods are stored below ready-to-eat foods so juices cannot drip onto them.

options.text: A step taken to fix a problem when a standard is not met

knowledgeCheck.explanation: Corrective actions fix the problem and prevent unsafe food from being served.

options.text: They must be changed when soiled or when tasks change, and hands must be washed first
They can be worn all shift

knowledgeCheck.explanation: Gloves are a barrier, not a substitute for handwashing, and must be changed between tasks.

exitTicket.prompt: Describe a food safety problem you have seen or could see in a kitchen, the risk it creates, and the corrective action.
